blocks.text: Datasets derived from each recording (one file → several queryable layers): content (transcript, sealed by sha); timing (start/end, pcm offsets); speaker-local label + corpus cluster id; condition (codec/rate/channels); discoverable spectrum columns; codec tokens (content stream cb0, character stream cb1-7).

Discoverable-spectrum columns (14): duration_s, chars_per_s, energy_db_mean, energy_db_std, pause_ratio, f0_mean_hz, f0_std_semitones, f0_range_hz, voiced_ratio, spectral_centroid_hz, spectral_bandwidth_hz, spectral_rolloff_hz, spectral_flatness, zcr.
Split rule: speaker-cluster-disjoint; straddling sessions → train; admission 10% / dev 10% by cluster hash.

Classification-driven exclusions: raw audio never leaves the host (raw_media_exported=false); transcripts stay on the host (text_exported=false); presenter identity is a corpus-local cluster id — no voiceprint is stored; the sealed admission split is never read by training.

Dev requalification (admission untouched): kik: 166 → 2962 segments (30 with brand mentions; 41 sessions promoted, dev_basis=session_holdout); kam: 2 → 3810 segments (30 with brand mentions; 75 sessions promoted, dev_basis=session_holdout); swa: 329 → 583 segments (37 with brand mentions; 4 sessions promoted, dev_basis=session_holdout).

This run read (from the host state before it ended): train_segments 81432, train_hours 67.22, dev_segments 261, text_vocab 68, admission_read False, per_language {'kik': 32180, 'kam': 16295, 'swa': 32957}.

Codec: kyutai/mimi revision 89091b3e466eb6a9d11e537bf26b144f194978f7, 8 codebooks × 12.5 Hz = 100.0 tokens/s; content stream codebook 0 (semantic, WavLM-distilled), character stream codebooks 1-7 (acoustic residual).

Starting model: none — the codec language model is trained from scratch on the database tokens; there is no pretrained voice and no presenter is cloned (AIP §§6–7). Pretrained MMS-TTS voices exist for Kikuyu and Kiswahili as comparators only; none exists for Kikamba.

Recipe (this iteration): lr = 0.0003, batch_size = 48, max_steps = 40000, warmup_steps = 1000, eval_every = 2500, checkpoint_every = 500, d_model = 768, layers = 12, heads = 12, max_segment_seconds = 12.0, spectral_feedback = True, eval_prompts_per_language = 12, comparators_per_language = 300, identity_cosine_threshold = 0.4.

Training: a codec language model (text characters → delayed Mimi frames, eight codebooks) trained from scratch. Rendered dev prompts are measured with the same discoverable-spectrum columns as the corpus; the per-feature divergence between generated and baseline distributions is the spectral-behaviour similarity, and where it is shifted the next curriculum up-weights the under-covered side of that feature (spectral feedback). The identity gate embeds each rendering and requires its cosine to every corpus-derived speaker comparator to stay below the threshold; comparators live in memory only.

No ablations were run in this settlement. The controlled same-base comparison of spectral-feedback curricula (MA-16) is a separate commission and is not claimed here.
Results are on the dev split, which guides iteration; they are not admission evidence. Admission is decided only on the sealed, speaker-cluster-disjoint split by a separate evaluation run.

The dev split was requalified after the cluster-disjoint rule left it too small to measure: whole train sessions were promoted to dev (dev_basis=session_holdout), so presenter voices may overlap between train and dev. This is a disclosed selection effect on dev; the admission split is unchanged.

Spectral-behaviour similarity is an instrument, not naturalness: a rendering can match the corpus distributions and still sound wrong. Native-listener ratings on unseen stories are required and are recorded as pending.
The identity gate is scoped to corpus-derived speaker representations of this estate; it is not a claim of global uniqueness over all humans.
No pretrained Kikamba voice exists as a comparator; the Kikamba baseline is the corpus distribution alone.
